composition_label: Journey recommendations -> Adaptive onboarding -> Ticket triage & routing -> Sentiment & prioritization

construction.implementation_origin: Written from scratch in the isolated build directory.

shared_schema.input: Exact fields: schema_version=1, synthetic=true, profile, actions, tickets, routing. See example_input.json for the complete synthetic fixture.
shared_schema.profile: experience: beginner/intermediate/expert; preferences: ordered unique strings including optional format and interest tags; completed: unique known action IDs.
shared_schema.actions: Unique id, title, prerequisite IDs, tags, format (video/text/interactive), integer difficulty 1..3. All prerequisites must exist; cycles are rejected.
shared_schema.tickets: Unique id, nonempty text, known action_id, severity (low/medium/high/critical). Empty ticket lists are valid.
shared_schema.routing: Ordered rules with unique category, single-word keywords, priority and nonempty accountable owner; fallback has category/priority/owner.
shared_schema.output: Envelope: schema_version, status, stage, input snapshot, accumulated results keyed by journey/adaptive/triage/sentiment.
shared_schema.validation: The shared validate boundary checks exact envelope keys, input, stage order and deterministic expected output for every preceding stage before accepting a handoff. Public orchestration is run(data) or advance(envelope, stage).
shared_schema.errors: CLI emits one JSON object with status=error and exit 2 on file, decoding, JSON or schema validation errors. Duplicate JSON keys and nonfinite constants are rejected.

cross_stage_handoffs.data: Validated two ordered action IDs, scores, explanations and satisfied prerequisites become onboarding modules without reordering.
Validated module action IDs and experience/preference choices become per-ticket onboarding context; active onboarding imposes a medium priority floor.
Validated routed tickets preserve text, action ID, severity, category, accountable owner, baseline priority and onboarding context in ranked issues.

behavior.journey: Eligible uncompleted actions score 3 per preference match minus difficulty distance from experience target. Descending score then ascending action ID determines order. Reevaluate prerequisites after the first planned step to produce exactly two steps; impossible two-step plans fail explicitly. Planned completion is hypothetical, never persisted as actual completion.
behavior.adaptive: Beginner uses guided depth, intermediate standard, expert fast-track. First recognized format preference wins, otherwise the catalog format. Format selection is a reference presentation preference, not an assertion that external media exists.
behavior.triage: Case-insensitive alphabetic token matching; most distinct matching keywords wins; configuration order breaks ties. No match uses fallback. Priority is the maximum of configured priority, reported severity and onboarding floor.
behavior.sentiment: Transparent English lexicon and per-token contribution records. Immediately preceding not/never/no reverses polarity. Sum determines positive/neutral/negative. Score <= -2 raises baseline one level capped at critical. Positive sentiment never reduces severity. Sort by descending final priority, ascending sentiment score, then ticket ID.
behavior.determinism: No clock, random generator, persistence, network or provider influences results. Caller input is deep-copied.
behavior.llm: No LLM step is needed or implemented.

included: One integrated CLI pipeline and shared validated envelope
Synthetic fixture and deterministic reference policies
Prerequisite validation, explanatory recommendations and two-step planning
Auditable sentiment and severity-aware ranked issues
Unit, handoff-tampering and real CLI subprocess tests
excluded: Enterprise operations, authentication, databases and UI
External providers, live data and external dependencies
Semantic or multilingual sentiment, sarcasm and long-range negation
Executing actions, actual ticket delivery, or actual media generation
Model training and optional LLM injection

cli.stdout: One JSON object with status=ok and stage=sentiment
cli.error_contract: Missing file, directory and missing arguments return one error JSON object and exit 2; malformed JSON, duplicate keys, nonfinite constants and invalid schemas also tested.
